images.caption: Statue of a Lion, part of two of the same statues. Placed at the entrance of the Postoffice building at the Neude in Utrecht. Both statues as well as the seven statues on the inside of the building where made by Hendrik A. van den Eynde between 1917 and 1924. The lions where in essence no part of the actual design, but where added on behalf of the citizen of Utrecht

images.caption: POST, TELEGRAPH and TELEPHONE building, Neude, Utrecht, The Netherlands. Interior Art Deco wall decoration inspired by Egyptian and Assyrian art. A large statue of black Belgian Petit Granit that represents a continent, with symbolic insulators of telegraph cables made of the same black Petit Granit above it on the left and right and above that in yellow stone columns of flying carrier pigeons. Prism glass in the curved long windows.

images.caption: Hoofdpostkantoor, the former main post office in Utrecht. It was built in 1920, which was the last Dutch post office to be closed in 2011. On 23 April 2020, the new Broese Booksellers store was opened here by writer Ronald Giphart. The Central Library of Utrecht is also housed in the building. It was opened to the public on 11 May 2020. PTT Telecom used to be a co-user of this building. Offices and an amplifier station were located here, where the long-distance connections came together.In the 1990s, a large part of the telephone traffic in the province of Utrecht and the Betuwe was handled via this location.
images.alt: Hoofdpostkantoor, the former main post office in Utrecht. It was built in 1920, which was the last Dutch post office to be closed in 2011. On 23 April 2020, the new Broese Booksellers store was opened here by writer Ronald Giphart. The Central Library of Utrecht is also housed in the building. It was opened to the public on 11 May 2020. PTT Telecom used to be a co-user of this building. images.caption: The Dom Tower in Utrecht, the Netherlands is one of the best known landmarks of this country. This gothic tower is the highest church tower (112,5 metres/368 feet) in the Netherlands and was built between 1321 and 1382 as part of the Cathedral of St. Martin. The resolution of the original photograph is 7768*4150.
